title: Optimizing Treatment of Cystoid Macular Edema in Pediatric Inherited Retinal Disease
official: Optimizing Treatment of Cystoid Macular Edema in Pediatric Inherited Retinal Disease
summary: The best treatment option for cystoid macular edema (CME) in children with inherited retinal disease (IRD) is not known. The purpose of this study is to investigate two potential eye drops which are used in the treatment CME to determine which is most helpful to pediatric participants in decreasing edema. All participants will be randomized to receive one of two possible study drugs and use them in one or both eyes for a period of up to 6 months.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Males or females age 3 to 12 years
2. Diagnosis of inherited retinal degeneration with molecular confirmation of disease (i.e. proven disease-causing variants in genes that are associated with the participant's clinical phenotype) from a Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA)-certified lab
3. Cystoid macular edema (CME) as judged by the investigator on SD-OCT that is treatment naive or currently untreated at time of enrollment
4. Female subjects ≥ 11 years of age must have a negative urine/serum pregnancy test.
5. Parental/guardian permission (informed consent) and if appropriate, child assent.
6. Reasonably able to cooperatively complete study procedures without use of sedation/anesthesia including SD-OCT and fluorescein angiography

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Subjects who have previously failed either investigational medication class (topical or oral CAI or topical NSAID)
2. Subjects currently receiving treatment for IRD-related CME, regardless of medication class
3. Subjects with x-linked retinoschisis (XLRS) due to mutation in retinoschisin1 (RS1) gene
4. Hypersensitivity to any of the investigational drugs
5. Hypersensitivity to fluorescein including if previously administered IV or PO
6. Any history of corneal denervation due to infection or surgical intervention
7. Diabetes mellitus (type 1 or 2)
8. Ocular surface disease (i.e. dry eye syndrome, Sjogren syndrome)
9. Rheumatoid arthritis
10. Clinically significant ocular surface changes (i.e. punctate epithelial erosions) due to contact lens wear upon screening and/or unwilling to discontinue contact lens use during trial period
11. Intraocular surgery within prior 6 months
12. History of bleeding tendencies or concomitant medications that prolong bleeding time
13. Moderate to severe renal disease defined as estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) \<60 milliliters(mL)/min/1.73m² using an age-appropriate formula
14. Pregnant or lactating female subjects
15. Subjects unwilling or unable to complete study procedures
